title: G2.2 - Recoverable Run execution
intent: Make Run execution recoverable and fenced across failure, retry, cancellation, and delayed callbacks.
scope: Implement Workspace-scoped RunAttempt, ExecutionLease, monotonic RunEvent cursor, fencing, observable cancellation, retry, RunWorkflow orchestration, read model, and Runs UI for the HostTrusted local execution slice.
non_goals: Implement remote Execution Gateway or Runner Fleet enrollment and transport
Claim ContainerIsolated, PrivateIsolated, KubernetesJob, or enterprise strong-isolation readiness
Implement IntegrationRun, HumanWorkResult, Artifact, Evidence, Submission, Review, or Acceptance closure
Replace inherited Paperclip heartbeat execution or Adapter implementations
Approve, merge, deploy, release, or create a ship record without independent review
acceptance_criteria: Run, RunAttempt, ExecutionLease, and RunEvent contracts are synchronized across DB, shared types, Go Domain API, TypeScript read model, and UI.
Each Attempt fixes Run, DeploymentRevision, AgentVersion, RuntimeProfile, executor identity, and a monotonically increasing fencing token.
An active lease can be claimed and heartbeated; expiry permits a new Attempt while stale tokens cannot advance authoritative state.
RunEvent cursors are monotonic, duplicate delivery is idempotent, and gaps are explicitly rejected and audited.
Completion, failure, retry, and observable cancellation advance RunAttempt, Run, and WorkNode only through domain commands.
RunWorkflow uses a stable ID, versioned signals, retry-safe commands, cancellation coordination, replay-safe state, and Continue-As-New.
The Runs surface shows Attempts, lease, fencing, cursor, cancellation, retry, and failure state; migration, tests, replay, typecheck, build, and browser fault acceptance pass.
